To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

1) the MCA and LIA had different impacts in the three regions, but in general they had negative consequences on the human population; 2) the MCA was a time of spatial rearrangements in the human populations; 3) these changes were associated with a reduction of population density in the Puna and Cuyo, and an increase in Patagonia; 4) the changes in the Puna were associated with the development of the Tiwanaku state;
the MCA was a period of population increase and economic expansion, while the LIA was characterized by a population contraction and economic recession.
